why: The student writes a valid if / else if / else chain that covers all three branches in order. But they changed `x > 0` to `x >= 0`, so x = 0 now prints "pos" instead of "zero", and the `zero` branch can never run. That is one slip in an otherwise rule-correct restructuring, so it is a multistructural error, not L0. It fails the "without changing what it prints" requirement, so it can't reach L3 or L4.
